official_measurement_examples: CROW rights normally apply to mapped open country and registered common land subject to exceptions
open access gives recreation rights rather than ownership
excepted land can remain without CROW access even inside mapped areas
public rights of way crossing access land are a separate legal right
restrictions and exclusions can change access availability temporarily
land being developed can become excepted land under CROW rules
development on open access land remains subject to planning approval
CROW status does not establish title access for vehicles or development yield
core_rules: CROW access is not public right of way
public right of way is distinct from CROW access
mapped access land can contain excepted land
restriction is not permanent loss of ownership
development status can alter access treatment
CROW rights do not grant vehicle access
CROW rights do not grant planning permission
planning permission does not itself extinguish all access rights
section16 dedication has distinct permanence rules
map status must retain date and restriction context
access authority is not title authority
access right does not calculate development yield
no parcel CROW clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Natural England, GOV.UK and CROW Act sources checked 2026-07-26. November 2025 revised management/restriction guidance and open-access/PROW/ownership separation retained; no parcel promotion.
